title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 1:1
body: “Great and admirable is the dignity of an Apostle, and we find Paul constantly setting forth the causes of it, not as if he took the honor to himself, but as intrusted with it, and being under the necessity of so doing. For when he speaks of himself as "called," and that "by the will of God," and again elsewhere, "a necessity is laid upon me" (1 Cor.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 1
bodyEs: “Grande y admirable es la dignidad de un apóstol, y hallamos a Pablo exponiendo constantemente las causas de ella, no como si tomara para sí el honor, sino como quien lo tiene confiado, y está bajo la necesidad de hacerlo. Porque cuando habla de sí mismo como «llamado», y eso «por la voluntad de Dios», y otra vez en otra parte, «me es impuesta necesidad» (1 Cor.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 1:5
body: “Nothing is so injurious to mankind as to undervalue friendship ; and not to cultivate it with the greatest care; as nothing, on the other hand, is so beneficial, as to pursue it to the utmost of our power. This Christ has shown, where He says, "If two of you shall agree on earth, as touching anything that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of My Father" (Matt.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 2
bodyEs: “Nada es tan dañino para la humanidad como menospreciar la amistad, y no cultivarla con el mayor cuidado; como nada, por otra parte, es tan provechoso como buscarla hasta el límite de nuestro poder. Esto lo ha mostrado Cristo, donde dice: «si dos de vosotros se convinieren en la tierra, de toda cosa que pidieren, les será hecho por mi Padre» (Mat.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 1:12
body: “The advantages arising from humility are generally acknowledged, and yet it is a thing not easily to be met with. There is affectation of humble talking enough and to spare, but humbleness of mind is nowhere to be found.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 3
bodyEs: “Las ventajas que nacen de la humildad se reconocen en general, y sin embargo es cosa que no se encuentra con facilidad. Hay afectación de hablar con humildad de sobra, pero la humildad de mente no se halla en ninguna parte.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 2:1
body: “The Priest is the common father, as it were, of all the world; it is proper therefore that he should care for all, even as God, Whom he serves. For this reason he says, "I exhort therefore that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men." From this, two advantages result.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 6
bodyEs: “El sacerdote es el padre común, por así decir, de todo el mundo; conviene, pues, que cuide de todos, aun como Dios, a quien sirve. Por esta razón dice: «Amonesto pues, ante todas cosas, que se hagan rogativas, oraciones, peticiones, hacimientos de gracias, por todos los hombres». De esto resultan dos ventajas.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 2:2
body: “If in order to put an end to public wars, and tumults, and battles, the Priest is exhorted to offer prayers for kings and governors, much more ought private individuals to do it. For there are three very grievous kinds of war.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 7
bodyEs: “Si para poner fin a las guerras públicas, y a los tumultos, y a las batallas, se exhorta al sacerdote a ofrecer oraciones por los reyes y los gobernantes, mucho más deben hacerlo los particulares. Porque hay tres clases muy penosas de guerra.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 2:8
body: “Moral. What? Dost thou approach God to pray, with broidered hair and ornaments of gold? Art thou come to a dance?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 8
bodyEs: “Moral. ¿Qué? ¿Te acercas a Dios para orar, con el cabello trenzado y adornos de oro? ¿Has venido a un baile?”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 3:1
body: “As now proceeding to discourse of the Episcopal office, he sets out with showing what sort of a person a Bishop ought to be. And here he does not do it as in the course of his exhortation to Timothy, but addresses all, and instructs others through him.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 10
bodyEs: “Como pasa ahora a discurrir del oficio episcopal, empieza mostrando qué clase de persona debe ser un obispo. Y aquí no lo hace como en el curso de su exhortación a Timoteo, sino que se dirige a todos, e instruye a otros por medio de él.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 3:8
body: “Discoursing of Bishops, and having described their character, and the qualities which they ought to possess, and having passed over the order of Presbyters, he proceeds to that of Deacons. The reason of this omission was, that between Presbyters and Bishops there was no great difference.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 11
bodyEs: “Discurriendo de los obispos, y habiendo descrito su carácter, y las cualidades que deben poseer, y habiendo pasado por alto el orden de los presbíteros, pasa al de los diáconos. La razón de esta omisión fue que entre presbíteros y obispos no había gran diferencia.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 4:1
body: “As those who adhere to the faith are fixed on a safe anchor, so those who fall from the faith can nowhere rest; but after many wanderings to and fro, they are borne at last into the very gulf of perdition.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 12
bodyEs: “Como los que se adhieren a la fe están fijos en un ancla segura, así los que caen de la fe no pueden descansar en ninguna parte; sino que, después de muchos vagabundeos de un lado a otro, son llevados al fin al abismo mismo de la perdición.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 4:11
body: “In some cases it is necessary to command, in others to teach; if therefore you command in those cases where teaching is required, you will become ridiculous. Again, if you teach where you ought to command, you are exposed to the same reproach.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 13
bodyEs: “En algunos casos es necesario mandar, en otros enseñar; si, pues, mandas en aquellos casos donde se requiere enseñar, te volverás ridículo. Otra vez, si enseñas donde debes mandar, quedas expuesto al mismo reproche.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 5:8
body: “Many consider that their own virtue is sufficient for their salvation, and if they duly regulate their own life, that nothing further is wanting to save them. But in this they greatly err, which is proved by the example of him who buried his one talent, for he brought it back not diminished but entire, and just as it had been delivered to him.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 14
bodyEs: “Muchos consideran que su propia virtud basta para su salvación, y que, si regulan debidamente su propia vida, no falta nada más para salvarlos. Pero en esto yerran mucho, lo cual se prueba con el ejemplo de aquel que enterró su único talento, porque lo devolvió no disminuido sino entero, y tal como se le había entregado.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 5:11
body: “For they had enrolled themselves on higher views, and the work with them proceeded from a greater elevation of mind. Therefore the receiving of strangers, and the washing of the Saints' feet, he has represented by "attending upon the Lord without distraction" (1 Cor.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 15
bodyEs: “Porque se habían inscrito con miras más altas, y la obra en ellas procedía de una elevación mayor de mente. Por eso el recibir a los extraños, y el lavar los pies de los santos, lo ha representado por «para que sin impedimento os lleguéis al Señor» (1 Cor.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 5:21
body: “Having spoken of Bishops and Deacons, of men, and women, of widows and elders, and of all others, and having shown how great was the authority of a Bishop, now he was speaking of judgment, he has added, "I charge thee before God and the Lord Jesus Christ and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality." Thus fearfully he charges him.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 16
bodyEs: “Habiendo hablado de obispos y diáconos, de hombres y mujeres, de viudas y ancianos, y de todos los demás, y habiendo mostrado cuán grande era la autoridad de un obispo, ahora que hablaba del juicio, ha añadido: «Te requiero delante de Dios y del Señor Jesucristo, y de sus ángeles escogidos, que guardes estas cosas sin perjuicio de nadie, que nada hagas inclinándote á la una parte». Así de temible es el cargo que le hace.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 6:2
body: “A teacher has need not only of authority, but of gentleness, and not only of gentleness, but of authority. And all these the blessed Paul teaches, at one time saying, "These things command and teach" (1 Tim.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 17
bodyEs: “Un maestro necesita no solo autoridad, sino mansedumbre, y no solo mansedumbre, sino autoridad. Y todo esto lo enseña el bienaventurado Pablo, diciendo a veces: «Esto manda y enseña» (1 Tim.”

title: John Chrysostom on 1 Timothy 6:13
body: “Again he calls God to witness, as he had done a little before, at once to increase his disciple's awe, and to secure his safety, and to show that these were not human commandments, that receiving the commandment as from the Lord Himself, and ever bearing in mind the Witness before Whom he heard it, he may have it more fearfully impressed upon his mind.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 18
bodyEs: “Otra vez llama a Dios por testigo, como había hecho poco antes, a la vez para aumentar el temor reverente de su discípulo, y para asegurar su seguridad, y para mostrar que estos no eran mandamientos humanos, a fin de que, recibiendo el mandamiento como del Señor mismo, y teniendo siempre en la mente al Testigo ante quien lo oyó, lo tenga impreso en la mente con más temor.”
